tool.name: AegisReview
tool.model: Google Gemini (some responses reused from cache)

executive_summary: The CDF TaskFlow application contains several critical security vulnerabilities that expose sensitive data and allow unauthorized control over the system. The most severe issues involve a raw SQL injection vulnerability in the search feature and architectural flaws in backend functions that allow attackers to modify or view any task and user profile in the database. Furthermore, a privilege escalation bug allows standard users to grant themselves administrative rights. These issues represent a significant risk to data integrity and privacy, requiring immediate remediation before the application is used in any production environment.
overall_assessment:
The overall security posture of the project is poor. There is a systemic failure to implement secure authorization patterns, particularly in the Deno Edge Functions where administrative 'service role' keys are used to bypass database security without implementing alternative identity checks. This, combined with high-risk coding practices like raw SQL interpolation and unsafe HTML rendering, makes the application highly vulnerable to multiple classes of attack.

Remediation should focus on securing the data access layer first. This includes fixing the SQL injection in the search function and replacing the insecure Edge Function authorization logic. Following this, database Row Level Security (RLS) policies should be tightened to enforce proper project-based isolation, and front-end rendering should be secured against XSS.
top_priorities: Refactor the 'search-tasks' function to use parameterized queries instead of raw SQL string interpolation.
Implement JWT validation and identity-based authorization checks in all Edge Functions, especially those using service role keys.
Modify the 'profiles' update policy to restrict users from updating the 'role' column.
Implement HTML sanitization for task comments to prevent stored XSS attacks.
Restrict Row Level Security (RLS) for the 'tasks' and 'profiles' tables to follow the principle of least privilege.

findings.title: SQL Injection in search-tasks function
findings.evidence:
const query = `
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE '%${searchTerm}%'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;

    const tasks = await sql.unsafe(query);
findings.description: The search term is concatenated directly into a SQL query string and executed using the 'unsafe' method of the postgres library. This allows an attacker to manipulate the query and potentially extract data from any table in the database.
findings.impact: An attacker can perform arbitrary database queries, leading to full data exfiltration from the tasks table and potentially other tables in the database.
findings.remediation: Use tagged template literals provided by the postgres library to safely parameterize the query instead of string concatenation and 'unsafe'.
findings.secure_code: const tasks = await sql`SELECT id, title, description, status FROM public.tasks WHERE title ILIKE ${'%' + searchTerm + '%'} ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 25`;

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) and Authentication Bypass in update-task
findings.description: The function uses the Supabase service role key to bypass all Row Level Security (RLS) and does not verify the identity or authorization of the requester. Any user, or even an unauthenticated attacker, can provide an arbitrary taskId and changes to update any task in the system.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of any task, including changing its title, description, status, or even ownership.
findings.remediation: Initialize the Supabase client with the user's own JWT from the 'Authorization' header and verify the user's identity using 'supabase.auth.getUser()'. Ensure RLS is enforced or manually check that the requesting user owns the task before updating.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in TaskComments
findings.description: User-supplied comment text is rendered directly as raw HTML using 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML' without any sanitization. This allows an attacker to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript by submitting a comment containing malicious HTML tags or attributes.
findings.impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary scripts in the browsers of other users who view the comment, potentially stealing session tokens or performing actions on behalf of the user.
findings.remediation: Avoid using 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML' for user-controlled text. Render the text as standard React children which are automatically escaped.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in get-profile
findings.evidence:
const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from("profiles")
      .select("*")
      .eq("id", userId)
      .single();
findings.description: The function retrieves user profile data based on a user-supplied 'userId' parameter without verifying if the requester is authenticated or authorized to access that profile. The use of 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY' explicitly bypasses Row Level Security.
findings.impact: Any user or anonymous visitor can retrieve the full profile information (including potential sensitive defaults) of any user by guessing or obtaining their UUID.
findings.remediation: Implement authentication using the Supabase client's auth.getUser(jwt) method and restrict profile access based on the authenticated user's context, or use the user's own token to initialize the client.

findings.title: Privilege Escalation via Profile Update Policy
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid());
findings.description: The update policy for the profiles table only checks if the user is the owner of the profile, but it does not restrict which columns can be updated. Since the profiles table contains a 'role' column, any user can update their own role from 'member' to 'admin'.
findings.impact: A regular user can escalate their privileges to administrator status, gaining unauthorized access to admin features.
findings.remediation: Modify the 'WITH CHECK' clause to ensure the 'role' column is not modified unless the user is already an admin, or use a database trigger to prevent role changes.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (
  id = auth.uid() 
  AND role = (SELECT role FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid())
);

findings.title: Excessive Data Exposure in Task RLS Policy
findings.description: The Row Level Security policy for the 'tasks' table allows any authenticated user to view all tasks in the database regardless of project membership or ownership. This violates the principle of least privilege.
findings.impact: Authenticated users can see tasks belonging to projects they do not own or are not members of, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.
findings.remediation: Restrict the SELECT policy for tasks to only those where the user is the owner or is a member of the associated project.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (owner_id = auth.uid() OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.projects WHERE projects.id = tasks.project_id AND projects.owner_id = auth.uid()));

findings.title: Permissive CORS Policy
findings.description: The function uses a wildcard ('*') for the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.
findings.impact: This allows any website to make requests to the edge function, increasing the surface for cross-site attacks if the endpoint is not otherwise properly protected.
findings.remediation: Restrict allowed origins to the specific domains used by the application.

findings.title: Overly Permissive Row Level Security (Profiles)
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view profiles"
ON public.profiles
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (true);
findings.description: The RLS policy allows any authenticated user to view all records in the profiles table.
findings.impact: This leads to information disclosure where any registered user can scrape the full list of users and their profile details.
findings.remediation: Restrict the policy so users can only view their own profile or profiles associated with their projects.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid());

findings.title: Hardcoded credential-like value
findings.description: A hardcoded API key for an analytics service was found in the configuration file. Hardcoding credentials in source code is a security risk as they are checked into version control.
findings.impact: If this is a production key, an attacker could abuse the analytics account, leading to data manipulation or financial costs.
findings.remediation: Move the API key to an environment variable (e.g., VITE_ANALYTICS_KEY) and access it via import.meta.env.
findings.validation_notes: Confirm if this is a real production key or a placeholder for development.

findings.title: Insecure Configuration: Debug Mode Enabled
findings.description: Verbose debugging is enabled in the configuration, which is dangerous if deployed to production.
findings.impact: Excessive logging can expose sensitive internal state, data, or application logic to anyone with access to the console or log output.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode by default and use environment variables to toggle it only for development environments.

findings.title: Information Disclosure (Sensitive Error Details)
findings.description: The function returns the raw error string to the client in the event of an exception.
findings.impact: This may reveal internal system details, such as database schema information or stack traces, which can aid an attacker in further exploits.
findings.remediation: Log the error internally and return a generic error message to the client.
